title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Training Note: Removed Dependents under a Child Support Order
content:
**Does a removed dependent still count after a dependency disallowance?** On an Unemployment Benefit Claims record, a removed dependent can still be counted at a share when a child support order binds the claimant. The record read is the claimant's Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders: every order of the kind Child Support Withholding — Current Support Order binding the claimant, on any of the claimant's claims, and the status of each.

| Child Support Withholding — Current Support Orders binding the claimant | Removed dependent counted at |
|---|---|
| At least one stands at status active or suspended | 0.5 (the supported share) |
| None stands active or suspended, and at least one has been received and stands at status requested | 0.25 (the pending-order share) |
| None stands at any of those statuses | No share |

**How does the share enter the allowance?** The share is added to the dependents now on record, and the total counted is no more than the program's maximum number of dependents; the per-dependent amount is multiplied by that count.

**Does a Child Support Withholding — Arrears-Only Order count?** No; the rule reads Current Support Orders only. An order at status revoked or terminated gives no share.

**Hypothetical cases.**

| Current Support Orders of the claimant | Share counted |
|---|---|
| One active order | 0.5 |
| One suspended order and one requested order | 0.5 |
| One requested order only | 0.25 |
| One terminated order and one requested order | 0.25 |
| One revoked order only | None |

With one dependent remaining on record and a share of 0.5, the dependents counted are 1.5; at a per-dependent amount of 15.00 the allowance computed is 22.50. With a share of 0.25 the count is 1.25 and the allowance 18.75.
